NOVELTY STATEMENT
Standard practice delivers: MONITORING/INDICATION scheme trending absolute volumetric efficiency η_v against a commissioned healthy baseline.  
My mechanism delivers: MONITORING/INDICATION scheme trending pressure-normalized slip coefficient C_slip = (Q_th − Q_act)/ΔP against a physics-derived threshold from nameplate specs.  
Failure-physics connection: Tip/end-plate wear increases clearance c; slip flow Q_slip ∝ c³·ΔP/μ for laminar leakage; thus C_slip = Q_slip/ΔP ∝ c³/μ grows monotonically with wear, independent of operating pressure fluctuations, providing a direct wear measure without a commissioned baseline.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing relation: Q_slip = (K·c³/μ)·ΔP (laminar flow in clearances, K = geometry constant) → C_slip = Q_slip/ΔP = K·c³/μ.  
Magnitude verification: For typical external gear pump at 60 cSt, 40 bar, η_v_rated ≈ 0.92 (catalog). Q_th = D·N. C_slip_rated = (1−η_v_rated)·Q_th/ΔP_rated = 0.08·Q_th/40 bar. At 8% η_v drop: η_v_crit = 0.92·η_v_rated = 0.8464. C_slip_crit = (1−η_v_crit)·Q_th/ΔP_rated = 0.1536·Q_th/40 bar. Ratio C_slip_crit/C_slip_rated = 1.92. Since C_slip ∝ c³, clearance increases by 1.92^(1/3) ≈ 1.24× (24% clearance growth) to reach the 8% η_v drop — consistent with wear progression to near-seizure. CALCULATED from stated specs: η_v_rated (catalog), D (nameplate), N (nameplate), ΔP_rated = 40 bar (USER CONSTRAINT), μ = 60 cSt (USER CONSTRAINT).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
| Component / Input | Source / Tag | Derivation / Note |
|---|---|---|
| Downstream flow Q_act | ALREADY-RECORDED (constraint: "downstream flow meter") | Direct sensor stream |
| Discharge pressure P_dis | ALREADY-RECORDED (constraint: "discharge pressure") | Direct sensor stream |
| Suction pressure P_suc | ALREADY-RECORDED (constraint: "suction pressure") | Direct sensor stream |
| Motor speed N | DERIVED (stated spec: motor nameplate rated speed) or ALREADY-RECORDED (if VFD frequency logged) | Constant or VFD signal; no new sensor |
| Pump displacement D | DERIVED (stated spec: pump nameplate) | Fixed geometry |
| Rated volumetric efficiency η_v_rated | DERIVED (stated spec: pump catalog/data sheet) | Published at 40 bar, 60 cSt |
| Compute platform | Existing plant historian / edge PLC (standard-practice bill) | No new hardware |
| Daily C_slip computation | Algorithm on existing platform | C_slip_daily = median[(D·N − Q_act)/(P_dis − P_suc)] over hours with ΔP > 20 bar (ASSUMPTION: minimum pressure for valid slip signal) and ≥4 hrs operation (ASSUMPTION: data quality filter) |
| Trend estimator | Theil-Sen slope on daily C_slip vs. time | Robust to outliers, no distributional assumption |
| Threshold C_slip_crit | CALCULATED from stated specs | C_slip_crit = (1 − 0.92·η_v_rated)·D·N / ΔP_rated |
| Alarm rule | Software configuration | Trigger when (C_slip_crit − C_slip_current) / slope ≤ 21 days (USER CONSTRAINT) |

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Installability: SAME — uses only existing sensors (suction/discharge pressure, flow meter, motor current available but not required) and existing historian/PLC; no wiring, no mounting.
- Operability: SAME — fully automated daily computation; no operator rounds, no manual entry.
- Maintenance: SAME — no added hardware to calibrate, clean, or replace.
- Cost class: SAME — software-only configuration change on existing infrastructure; zero capital, zero consumables.
- Operational loss: ZERO — no process interruption, no bypass, no recipe change.
- Conclusion: SAME burden class, DIFFERENT mechanism (physics-normalized slip coefficient with spec-derived threshold vs. baseline-dependent η_v trending).

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol:
1. Extract ≥12 months of ALREADY-RECORDED sensor data (Q_act, P_suc, P_dis, I_motor) from the target pump’s historian.
2. Compute daily median C_slip for each day with ≥4 operating hours at ΔP > 20 bar.
3. Fit Theil-Sen linear regression to C_slip vs. time (days since commissioning).
4. For each day, project days-to-threshold = (C_slip_crit − C_slip_current) / slope (slope > 0 required).
5. Flag alarm on any day where projected days-to-threshold ≤ 21.
6. Validate on this same recorded dataset against two criteria:
   a) FALSE ALARM RATE: Count alarms occurring in the first 50% of the pump’s recorded life (ASSUMPTION: low-wear period). PASS if ≤1 alarm per year of operation. FAIL if >1.
   b) LEAD TIME: If the recorded history contains a ≥8% η_v drop (η_v = Q_act/(D·N) evaluated at ΔP ≈ 40 bar), verify an alarm was triggered ≥21 days before that drop. PASS if yes. FAIL if no alarm or lead <21 days.
7. Kill criterion: FAIL on either (a) or (b) → predictor rejected; do not deploy.

CONSTRAINT BIND (predictor)
Primary stated indicator: Volumetric efficiency η_v (the constraint defines failure as "volumetric efficiency drops 8 percent" — η_v is the quantity whose threshold defines the failure). The predictor uses C_slip as a leading indicator that SUPPLEMENTS η_v by providing a pressure-normalized, physics-referenced wear trajectory; C_slip never replaces η_v — the 8% drop is defined on η_v, and C_slip_crit is derived from the η_v value corresponding to that drop. Motor current (available per constraint) is not required for the core predictor but may supplement speed verification if VFD data is absent.
